title: A day in the life of a torque wrench, told by the torque wrench
summary: A whimsical first-person note from a click-type torque wrench about calibration anxiety, over-torquers, and the one bolt that mattered.

blocks.title: I am a torque wrench, and today I clicked for a living
blocks.body: I live in a foam cutout that smells faintly of oil. Humans borrow me, set my numbers, and pretend the click is optional. It is not.

items.title: Crib checkout
items.detail: A hand with coffee breath writes my asset tag on a log. Flattering.

items.title: First truth
items.detail: Cylinder head bolts. I am set correctly. I click. Someone still leans 'just a hair more.' I forgive nothing.

items.title: Abuse attempt
items.detail: Used as a breaker bar. My soul leaves through the ratchet. A lead notices. I am rescued.

items.title: The careful one
items.detail: Slow pull, straight axis, stop on click. This is what calibration dreams about.

items.title: Return
items.detail: Wound back toward storage setting, wiped, logged OK. I sleep in foam. Tomorrow: another flange.

blocks.quote: The click is not a suggestion. It is the end of the sentence.

blocks.title: If you borrow me
blocks.body: Set me in my range, pull smooth, stop at click, never use me to bust frozen bolts, and put my spring near rest when you put me away. I will repay you with fasteners that stay where engineering put them.
